items.t: Choosing a dispensing system: the practical guide
items.d: What to clarify before investing: components, throughput, containers, Ex protection, storage and software.
h: Why an automatic dispensing system pays off
Step 1: Record components and raw materials
Step 4: Plan storage, pipes and agitation as well
items.x: A dispensing system is not an off-the-shelf machine. Two paint manufacturers with a similar range can need completely different systems – because the number of components, container sizes, throughput and space differ. This guide shows which points you should clarify before an enquiry and how to derive the right type of system from them. Why an automatic dispensing system pays off Anyone who weighs out recipes by hand knows the weak points: every component has to go on the scale individually, containers are opened and decanted, and the documentation is written afterwards. Errors often only show up during re-tinting or in quality control. An automatic dispensing system takes over the weighing according to the recipe, checks every quantity with a scale and stores every operation. The advantages users mention most often: Reproducible batches: every batch matches the previous one, because quantities do not depend on how the day is going. Small orders produced economically: even the smallest quantities can be made quickly and without set-up effort. Fewer open containers: raw materials come through pipes from the tank farm instead of being decanted. Complete documentation: the dispensing log shows what went into which batch and when. Step 1: Record components and raw materials The starting point is a list of all raw materials that are to be dispensed automatically. For each component, the following matter: Viscosity and flow behaviour: solvents, binders, pastes and additives behave very differently (see viscosity). Solids content: pigmented products tend to sedimentation and need recirculation or agitators. Reactivity: UV-curing or reactive substances place their own demands on storage and valves. Hazardous properties: flammable solvents require Ex protection. Annual consumption: it decides whether a substance comes from a stationary tank or from an exchangeable container. The number of components determines the size of the dispensing centre. Füll builds systems with just a few valves up to systems with 64 components and more. Step 2: Define throughput and containers The second question is: how much is dispensed per day – and into which containers? The smallest containers such as bottles need different systems than 200-litre drums or process vessels. Containers / throughput Typical Füll series Very small container openings (e.g. bottles), low throughput FS MS – valves in one row, the scale moves with the container Buckets and pails, low throughput, little space FS XS – valves in a circle, compact, Ex and non-Ex Buckets, 25 kg pails, medium throughput FS 2005.2 – up to 32 valves in two rows Pails, 200 L drums, process vessels, high throughput FS 182.2 – more than 32 valves Reactive components for downstream processes (laminating, coating) FS 188 – continuous and discontinuous feeding Laboratory and recipe development LX5 laboratory dispensing system Sales containers from a batch size of 1 In-can tinting The table is a first orientation. In the preliminary project planning, the design is matched to your process parameters. Step 3: Choose the measuring principle Gravimetric systems measure the mass with a scale or a mass flow meter. This is the standard when high reproducibility and traceability are required. Volumetric systems dispense a defined volume, for example with a piston pump, and are particularly fast, for instance when tinting into pre-filled containers. Both methods can be combined: Füll dispensing centres can be equipped with scales or with the volumetric dispensing unit HX5. You will find the detailed comparison in the guide Gravimetric or volumetric dispensing. Step 4: Plan storage, pipes and agitation as well A dispensing system is only as good as its supply of raw materials. Do the components come from stationary tanks, from containers in a rack or from exchangeable containers? Are they recirculated so that nothing settles? How do they get to the system? That is why Füll plans tank farms, pipes, recirculation and agitators together with the dispensing system. With a correct process design of the storage, the effort for rework such as re-tinting drops considerably. More on this in the guide Planning a tank farm. Step 5: Safety and regulations Solvent-based paints, coatings and printing inks almost always mean potentially explosive areas. Systems, terminals and agitators must then be designed according to ATEX. Storage areas with liquids hazardous to water are subject to the requirements of German water law (WHG), for example an approved overfill protection. Füll is certified according to ATEX for the manufacture of equipment and is a WHG specialist company. Details in the guide Ex protection for dispensing systems. Step 6: Software and connection The software manages orders, recipes, stocks and logs. At Füll this is CALIPSO, in use since 1993 and continuously developed further. Clarify in advance: Should orders and recipes come from the ERP or MES system (ERP connection)? Will colour measurement data be imported? Which access rights do operators, the laboratory and production need? How long must dispensing logs be kept for batch traceability? Checklist for your enquiry With this information, a manufacturer can draw up a reliable concept and quotation: List of components with viscosity, Ex classification and annual consumption Containers and batch sizes (smallest and largest quantity) Number of orders per day and required accuracy Existing storage, space, room height and Ex zones Desired connection to ERP, MES or colour measurement Budget and schedule How accurately does a dispensing system dispense? That depends on the scale, valve, target quantity and product. Depending on the version, Füll dispensing centres achieve a dispensing accuracy of up to 0.1 g. Can an existing dispensing system be extended? Yes. Thanks to the modular design, additional valves, pipes and storage containers can be retrofitted. A retrofit of older systems is also possible. How long does a system project take? That depends on the scope. A single system is implemented much faster than a complete project with a tank farm; the Sherwin-Williams project with a tank farm and several systems took around 18 months.

items.d: UV, solvent-based and water-based printing inks: choice of system, storage of reactive raw materials and a practical example.
items.x: Hardly any industry has as many shades, binder systems and printing processes as printing and packaging. Providing the inks is correspondingly demanding – especially with UV-curing printing inks. The challenge Flexo, gravure, offset, screen and pad printing, plus flexible packaging, labels, corrugated board and decor: every combination requires its own inks. On top of that come laminating adhesives, solvents and additives. Anyone who mixes special shades by hand loses time, material and reproducibility. Which system for which consumption? Requirement Solution at Füll Small to medium printing ink consumption, little space FS XS – the smallest fully automatic Füll dispensing centre Printing inks of low to medium viscosity, batches of 1–5 kg U-VX5 – even 100 g batches reproducibly Medium to high annual throughput, also very small containers FS 2005.2 and FS 182.2 These systems are suitable for water-based and solvent-based as well as for UV-curing products. With the FS XS, all components are recirculated via the valves to prevent sedimentation. Special case: UV-curing printing inks UV-curing inks and coatings contain reactive components that polymerise under UV radiation. For dispensing this means: Raw materials must not be exposed to UV light in storage or in the pipes. Many components are pasty and highly viscous; they often have to be temperature-controlled so that they remain pumpable. Valves must dispense highly viscous substances precisely without product dripping afterwards. Practical example: Zeller & Gmelin Zeller & Gmelin in Eislingen is one of the leading suppliers of radiation-curing printing inks. From 2013, Füll redesigned the production of these inks – from goods receipt via a UV-protected store heated to 38 °C and the piping system to dispensing. Planning began with a 3D model of the entire system. In several weeks of joint trials, both teams developed a new Aircut valve for the highly viscous, reactive substances. The system can be extended to up to 100 dispensing valves. In 2016, the state of Baden-Württemberg recognised the resource-saving handling of the raw materials. Instead of transporting 200-litre containers, pumps now convey the ink to the system. To the case study. Software for the printing company The dispensing software CALIPSO contains function modules for printing and packaging. In the dispensing log, operations can be sorted for example by order, motif/design, recipe or product. For volumetric systems in label printing there is the recipe management program AURORA, and for manual weighing AURORA-Mix as a cost-effective entry into dispensing technology. Is a system worthwhile for smaller printing companies? The FS XS was developed as a cost-effective alternative for very small to medium printing ink consumption, without compromising on quality and traceability. Can I start without a dispensing system? Yes. AURORA-Mix guides the operator through manual weighing together with a scale and is the cost-effective entry into dispensing technology.

items.t: Ex protection for dispensing systems: what matters
items.d: Why solvent-based products need Ex protection and what that means for the system, storage and operation.
h: What this means for the dispensing system
items.x: Anyone who dispenses solvent-based paints, coatings, printing inks or adhesives almost always works in potentially explosive areas. Explosion protection is then not an option but a prerequisite – for the dispensing system as well as for storage, agitators and terminals. Why explosion protection? Many solvents form vapours even at room temperature which, mixed with air, create an ignitable mixture. One ignition source – a spark, a hot surface, an electrostatic discharge – is enough. At Sherwin-Williams in El Salvador, explosion protection was a central requirement of the management, because some of the solvents used become critical at temperatures that are reached there every day. ATEX in brief In the EU, two directives regulate explosion protection (ATEX): The product directive 2014/34/EU applies to manufacturers of equipment and protective systems used in potentially explosive areas. The operator directive 1999/92/EC obliges employers to divide areas into zones according to the hazard and to use suitable equipment. For gases and vapours there are zones 0, 1 and 2 – from a permanent to a rare and short-term hazard. The operator defines which zone applies in the explosion protection document. What this means for the dispensing system All equipment in the zone must be suitable for it: valve drives, scales, agitators, terminals. Closed systems reduce vapours: raw materials come from tanks through pipes instead of from open containers. Earthing and equipotential bonding prevent electrostatic charging. Operator terminals are explosion-protected or placed outside the zone. Ex protection at Füll Füll holds an EC certificate according to Annex IV of Directive 2014/34/EU for the manufacture of various items of equipment, monitored by TÜV SÜD Product Service. Füll already received the manufacturing approval for agitators and level indicators according to ATEX in 2003. The compact dispensing centre FS XS is suitable for Ex and non-Ex environments. In the Sherwin-Williams project, all systems and equipment were built according to ATEX, and nine further dispensing systems were connected to a central control system with explosion-protected terminals. The result from the customer’s point of view: closed systems, more cleanliness and operational safety. Checklist for operators Explosion protection document and zone classification up to date? All components of the system suitable and marked for the zone? Closed storage and conveying wherever possible? Earthing concept for containers, scales and pipes? Maintenance by qualified personnel with Ex knowledge? Who defines the Ex zone? The operator, as part of the risk assessment and the explosion protection document. The system builder then designs the system for this zone. Are there Füll systems for Ex and non-Ex areas? Yes. The FS XS, for example, is suitable for both environments; larger systems are designed for the specific project.

items.t: Gravimetric or volumetric dispensing: which method when?
items.d: Mass or volume? Advantages and disadvantages of both methods, influencing factors and which system uses what.
items.x: Whether a dispensing system measures mass or volume determines accuracy, speed and traceability. Both methods have their place – and in many systems they are combined. The principle: mass or volume In gravimetric dispensing, the container stands on a scale. The valve opens until the target mass is reached. What is measured is therefore exactly what is written in the recipe – because recipes in the paint, coatings and chemical industries are usually given in mass fractions. In volumetric dispensing, a defined volume is delivered, for example by a piston pump. The mass is calculated from the density. Gravimetric: the strengths Independent of density and temperature: the scale measures the actual mass. High reproducibility: every addition is checked and logged. Flexible with many components: a dispensing centre can dispense many raw materials one after the other into the same container. Coarse and fine flow: first dispensing with a high flow rate, then only fine shortly before the target (coarse and fine flow dispensing). The disadvantage: components are usually dispensed one after the other. With many components per recipe, the process therefore takes longer than simultaneous dispensing. Volumetric: the strengths Simultaneous dispensing: several components at the same time, for example pigmented tinting pastes into a pre-filled container. Very fast with small quantities. No weighing set-up required. The disadvantage: deviations in density, air bubbles or temperature fluctuations have a direct effect on the mass. Many liquids expand measurably when heated – the same volume then contains less mass. Direct comparison Criterion Gravimetric Volumetric Measured variable Mass (scale, mass flow meter) Volume (piston pump, dispensing unit) Influence of density and temperature low high Sequence mostly one after the other also simultaneous Typical application Production from many raw materials and semi-finished products Tinting into pre-filled containers, small quantities Traceability every mass measured calculated, optionally checked gravimetrically Influencing factors in practice Accuracy does not only depend on the measuring principle. Just as important are: The dispensing valve: outlet size and design must match flow behaviour, density and viscosity. Füll adapts the valves individually to the substances to be dispensed. The valve drive: servo-driven valves open precisely and reproducibly. The homogeneity of the raw material: if pigment settles, the composition is wrong – no matter how accurately it is dispensed. That is why components are recirculated (recirculation). Run-on and drops at the valve tip, especially with viscous media. Combined solutions In many systems both principles work together. With Füll in-can tinting, the base is first added gravimetrically and then tinted volumetrically and simultaneously with pastes. The U-VX5 dispenses UV-curing inks simultaneously or under gravimetric control. The Füll dispensing centres FS 2005.2 and FS 182.2 can be equipped with scales or with the volumetric dispensing unit HX5. How to make the decision Many raw materials, production from semi-finished products, high traceability requirements: gravimetric. Tinting into pre-filled containers, high speed, few pastes: volumetric. Both in the same plant: a combined system or two types of system with shared software. Which method is more accurate? In terms of mass, gravimetric dispensing is usually more accurate because density and temperature play no role. Volumetric systems also achieve good values under constant conditions. Can you dispense volumetrically and still weigh? Yes. Volumetric dispensing can additionally be checked with a scale, so traceability is maintained.

items.t: Modernising a dispensing system: retrofit instead of a new build
items.d: Control system, servo drives, valve cleaning: which modernisations pay off – also for systems from other manufacturers.
h: When does a retrofit make sense?
items.x: A dispensing system is built for many years – a service life of 20 years is nothing unusual for Füll systems. Often it is only individual assemblies that need refreshing after a long service life. A retrofit is then a cost-effective alternative to a new build. When does a retrofit make sense? The control system or computer is outdated and spare parts are becoming scarce. Production or the product range has grown, and the system needs more valves or storage containers. The dispensing speed or accuracy is no longer sufficient. New requirements for documentation or ERP connection. Wear on heavily loaded assemblies. As with new systems, system safety has top priority. Füll defines the degree of modernisation together with the customer – and also offers retrofits for systems from other manufacturers. Electrical control system The computer stores system parameters, recipes, orders and logs. An industrial computer also ages and should be replaced after some time. Current control concepts communicate via Ethernet. This makes remote maintenance possible via secure VPN connections: service technicians can analyse the system down to the level of the PLC. Valve control and valve lift In the FS 182.2 and FS 2005.2 series, the valves are controlled by servo drives. This enables a dynamic, precise dispensing sequence; dispensing parameters are determined and optimised automatically by CALIPSO. After a power failure, no initialisation is needed. The valve lift is the most heavily loaded assembly of a dispensing centre, because it opens and closes all valves. For coarse and fine flow dispensing it has to work quickly and precisely. Valve carriage In most gravimetric systems, the valves sit on a carriage that moves the active valve under the lift by servo drive – usually at 250 mm/s. The same servo motors for lift and carriage simplify spare parts stocking, and the drive knows its position after a power failure. Automatic valve cleaning If manual cleaning of the valve heads does not always succeed during production peaks, automatic valve cleaning is worthwhile. Rotating brushes clean the valve heads with a suitable cleaning agent that is circulated. This protects against contamination and carry-over of residues and saves operating time. Extend instead of replace More products, higher capacity, new raw materials: thanks to the modular design of Füll systems, additional valves, pipes, hoses and storage containers can be integrated. At Zeller & Gmelin, for example, the system can be extended to up to 100 dispensing valves. Does Füll also modernise systems from other manufacturers? Yes, retrofit solutions are also available for products from other manufacturers. How does a retrofit work? First the system is analysed. Then Füll proposes measures – from a control upgrade to replacing complete assemblies and storage tanks. You decide on the scope.

items.d: Five types, electric or pneumatic, explosion-protected: which agitator suits which container.
items.x: Agitators ensure that raw materials remain homogeneous and that solids are kept in suspension. For dispensing systems they are a central part of storage technology – and depending on the container, a different type is suitable. Why an agitator in storage? Many raw materials of the paint, coatings and chemical industries do not stay homogeneous by themselves: pigments settle (sedimentation), dispersions separate. In combination with a recirculation line, an agitator ensures that every dispensed quantity has the same composition. This reduces later corrections such as re-tinting. The types at a glance Type Mounting Use Built-in agitator fixed from above on a nozzle or flange tanks and storage containers: homogenising, recirculating, keeping in suspension Lid agitator placed on an adapted container lid pails, drums, metal containers – stirring directly in the delivery container IBC agitator on a support above the IBC 1,000 L plastic IBCs, usually with a folding impeller Stand agitator free-standing, wall, floor/wall or mobile drums, containers, IBCs, small containers; lifting and lowering mostly pneumatic Special agitator customer-specific applications for which no standard type fits Electric or pneumatic? Agitator drives are available as electric and pneumatic versions. Pneumatic drives are widespread in potentially explosive areas because they work without an electrical ignition source at the drive. Electric drives can be controlled more finely and do not need compressed air. In the Ex area, both must be designed according to ATEX. Further features at Füll: anti-reach-through guard, automatic lifting device and a mobile version on castors. Selection criteria Container: delivery container (lid, IBC or stand agitator) or stationary tank (built-in agitator)? Opening: plastic IBCs have small openings, hence folding impellers. Viscosity and solids content of the product. Ex zone and hazardous substance classification. Frequency of change: if the agitator is moved often, top-mounted or stand solutions are more practical. Agitators from Füll Füll manufactures agitators and other equipment itself and has held the manufacturing approval for agitators according to ATEX since 2003. Since 2014 there has been a network of sales agents for agitator technology in Germany. The Füll sales team helps with the selection. More under Agitators. Can I stir directly in the delivery container? Yes, with a lid agitator, IBC agitator or stand agitator. This makes sense when there is no storage tank or a circulation line is not sufficient. Do I need a pneumatic agitator in the Ex area? Not necessarily. What matters is an ATEX-compliant design for the respective zone; pneumatic drives are common there, though.

items.t: Planning tank farms and storage systems for dispensing systems
items.d: Stationary or exchangeable containers, recirculation, agitators and water law: what matters in storage.
h: What types of storage are there?
How to find the right solution
items.x: The dispensing system is the visible heart of production. Whether it works reliably, however, is often decided by the storage in front of it: this is where raw materials are stocked, kept homogeneous and conveyed to the system. What types of storage are there? Füll distinguishes between stationary storage systems and exchangeable containers: Type of storage Examples Suitable for Stationary in a rack storage containers, cubic or cylindrical many components on little floor space Stationary free-standing cylindrical storage tanks, large tanks raw materials with high consumption, delivery by tanker Exchangeable containers buckets, pails, cans, drums, plastic and metal IBCs, round containers with follower plate or scraper low consumption, frequent changes of raw material How to find the right solution The design depends on consumption, delivery quantity, medium and the conditions on site. At Füll, a detailed analysis is carried out for this in the quotation phase – together with the operator and the raw material supplier. Typical questions: How much of each component is consumed per month? In which containers does the supplier deliver – and is delivery by tanker possible? Does the storage have to be temperature-controlled? At Zeller & Gmelin, the storage for UV printing ink raw materials is kept at a constant 38 °C and protected from UV light. How much space is available, and at what distance from the dispensing system? Homogeneity: recirculating and stirring Pigmented products and dispersions tend to sedimentation. Without countermeasures, the composition of the dispensed quantity is no longer correct. Two means ensure uniform raw materials: Recirculation: the product circulates through a ring line and the dispensing valves back into storage. For this, Füll dispensing valves have recirculation connections as standard. Agitators: they homogenise the contents of tanks, containers and drums. In the control software CALIPSO, recirculation and stirring intervals are defined and components are divided into groups. With a correct design, rework such as re-tinting is reduced considerably. Pump instead of carry A well-planned storage replaces manual transport. At Zeller & Gmelin, the ink used to be taken from storage to production in 200-litre containers; today pumps convey it through a piping system. This improves ergonomics, eliminates the risk of transport accidents and makes purchasing easier, because raw materials can be delivered by tanker. Safety and water law In Germany, storage for liquids hazardous to water is subject to water law. This includes, for example, approved overfill protection. Füll is a WHG specialist company and qualified to install safety-relevant system parts such as overfill protection. The level indicator FA 200/4 is approved as overfill protection according to WHG and ATEX. With flammable solvents, Ex protection is added – from the agitator to the terminal. Is a large tank farm worthwhile? With high consumption of individual raw materials, often yes: delivery by tanker, less container handling and less waste. At Sherwin-Williams, Füll handled the engineering for a large tank farm with 25- to 50-tonne tanks. Can I start with exchangeable containers? Yes. Many systems combine stationary tanks for the main raw materials with exchangeable containers for rarely used components.

items.d: The Aircut valve is a dispensing valve that Füll developed together with Zeller & Gmelin to dispense highly viscous substances accurately.
items.x: Pasty, highly viscous raw materials are difficult to dispense accurately: they flow slowly, form threads and can drip after the valve tip closes. With radiation-curing printing inks, the raw materials are also reactive and must be handled gently. For the production of radiation-curing printing inks at Zeller & Gmelin, both companies searched for the optimum dispensing solution in several weeks of joint trials. The result was a new Aircut valve that dispenses the highly viscous substances accurately.

items.d: ATEX refers to the European directives on explosion protection: 2014/34/EU for equipment and protective systems, 1999/92/EC for the protection of workers.
items.x: The name comes from the French “ATmosphères EXplosibles”. Manufacturers must prove that their equipment is safe for the intended zone; operators divide their areas into zones and use only suitable equipment. Füll holds an EC certificate according to Annex IV of Directive 2014/34/EU for the manufacture of various items of equipment, monitored by TÜV SÜD Product Service.

items.d: CALIPSO (Color And Liquid Processing Software) is Füll’s dispensing software, used to operate dispensing systems and manage orders, recipes, stocks and logs.
items.x: CALIPSO was introduced in 1993 and has been developed further ever since. The software environment consists of the PC interface, the software of the system control (PLC) and the user interface on the terminal. Standard features include order, recipe, container and scale management, recirculation and stirring intervals, material stock, a password system and dispensing and error logs. Interfaces to ERP systems or colour measurement are available as options. CALIPSO BATCH is designed for production from semi-finished products.

items.d: Batch traceability means being able to prove for every batch produced which raw materials were used, in what quantity, when and by whom.
items.x: It is the basis for complaint handling and quality management. In practice, it also matters that a customer can buy the same shade again years later. Automatic dispensing systems store every dispensing and filling operation in the dispensing log. In CALIPSO, the data can be queried and exported by period, component, order or product.

items.d: A lid agitator is a top-mounted agitator that is placed on an adapted container lid and stirs directly in the delivery container.
items.x: Lid agitators are used for pails, drums, metal containers and other containers with lids. They are built for quick changes: put on, lock, stir. In the storage systems of dispensing systems, they are used when there is no tank into which the contents can be transferred, or when a circulation line alone does not mix sufficiently.

items.d: Dispensing accuracy indicates how close the quantity actually dispensed is to the target quantity.
items.x: It depends on the measuring principle, scale, valve, valve drive, product and target quantity. The smaller the target quantity, the more absolute deviations matter. Depending on the version, Füll dispensing centres achieve a dispensing accuracy of up to 0.1 g. Reproducibility is just as important – that the same recipe is always dispensed in the same way.

items.d: The dispensing log is the automatic record of every dispensing and filling operation of a dispensing system.
items.x: Because every operation is stored, it is possible to trace later which order was processed with which recipe and which components. The log therefore serves quality assurance and batch traceability. In CALIPSO, the log can be sorted (for example by filling, order, motif/design, recipe or product), filtered and exported.

items.d: A dispensing valve releases a raw material in a controlled quantity from the supply line into the target container.
items.x: Füll dispensing valves are made of stainless steel and available with outlet sizes from 8 to 65 mm inner diameter; a 65 mm valve reaches flow rates of up to 5.97 m³/h. There are automatic valves – with a needle for ultra-fine dispensing, controlled pneumatically or by servo – as well as manual dispensing valves. As standard, the valves have recirculation connections. In every system, they are individually adapted to the flow behaviour, density and viscosity of the substances. With a free outlet, the manual dispensing valves even allow dispensing during a power failure.

items.d: A dispensing centre is the central part of a dispensing system, where the dispensing valves of all components are brought together and dispense into the target container.
items.x: Depending on the series, the valves are arranged in a circle, in one row or in two rows. In many gravimetric systems, a valve carriage moves the active valve under the valve lift; the scale measures the addition. Füll series range from the compact FS XS to the FS 182.2 with more than 32 valves.

items.d: ERP connection means that a dispensing system receives orders and recipes directly from the company’s ERP system.
items.x: This avoids duplicate entries and transmission errors. At Sherwin-Williams, all orders are loaded centrally from the ERP system to the Füll terminals; every work step is confirmed with a password. At Füll, every ERP interface is adapted to CALIPSO for the specific customer; data is transmitted via Ethernet. MES systems can also be connected.

items.d: Ex protection (explosion protection) covers all measures that prevent explosions in areas with flammable gases, vapours or dusts.
items.x: This includes avoiding an explosive atmosphere, for example through closed systems, avoiding ignition sources and design measures. In the EU, explosion protection is regulated by the ATEX directives. In dispensing systems for solvent-based products, explosion protection concerns valve drives, scales, agitators, terminals and the storage area.

items.d: Remote maintenance means that service technicians analyse and support a system via a secure data connection without being on site.
items.x: With current Füll controls, remote maintenance takes place via the internet and secure VPN tunnels. The technicians can analyse the system down to the control level of the PLC. Many questions can thus be clarified directly between service and production; a technician only comes on site when necessary.

items.d: A level indicator shows the fill level of a container and can also serve as overfill protection.
items.x: The Füll level indicator FA 200/4 is used in stationary, unpressurised containers of cubic design. It works on the float principle: a ball floats on the liquid and transmits the level to a scale via a rod and shaft. The FA 200/4 is approved as overfill protection according to the German Water Resources Act (WHG) and according to ATEX for flammable liquids.

items.d: Gravimetric dispensing means that the quantity added is measured by its mass – with a scale or a mass flow meter.
items.x: The method is independent of density and temperature and is therefore standard when recipes are given in mass fractions and high reproducibility is required. Automatic systems usually work with coarse and fine flow. Most Füll dispensing centres work gravimetrically, for example FS XS, FS MS, FS 2005.2 and FS 182.2. Depending on the application, the FS 188 uses scales or mass flow meters.

items.d: In coarse and fine flow dispensing, most of the quantity is first dispensed with a high flow rate and then accurately completed with a low flow rate shortly before the target.
items.x: This way the system combines speed with accuracy. Fast, precise valve movements and keeping to the stroke height for both phases are decisive. In Füll systems, the valve lift opens and closes all valves continuously; servo-controlled drives allow the dispensing parameters to be set precisely.

items.d: A semi-finished product is a prefabricated intermediate product, for example a pigment paste or a stock solution, from which the end product is made by mixing it with other components.
items.x: In paint and coatings production, end products are often made up of semi-finished products. This shortens production time and increases flexibility. For production from semi-finished products, Füll offers the dispensing software CALIPSO BATCH. At Sherwin-Williams, liquid semi-finished products are stored in closed tank systems.

items.d: An IBC is a large packaging for liquids, usually a 1,000-litre plastic container in a lattice cage on a pallet, or a metal container.
items.x: IBCs are a common delivery container for raw materials. In dispensing systems, they serve as exchangeable containers from which material is dispensed directly. Because plastic IBCs have only a small opening, IBC agitators with a folding impeller are usually used for stirring.

items.d: An IBC agitator (also called container or traverse agitator) is a top-mounted agitator fitted on a support for stirring in IBCs.
items.x: For 1,000-litre plastic IBCs, the support is designed as a crossbar that is locked onto the container. Because the opening is small, most IBC agitators have a folding impeller. IBC agitators are installed on an exchangeable container only for a short time and then moved on.

items.d: In-can tinting is the tinting of paints directly in the sales container as needed, from a batch size of one container.
items.x: Instead of keeping many shades in stock, the desired shade is only produced when it is needed. This reduces stocks and residual quantities. With the Füll system, the operator places a container with a barcode and releases it. The base is first added gravimetrically, then tinted volumetrically and simultaneously with universal pastes and finally stirred in a self-cleaning agitator. The degree of automation can be chosen freely.

items.d: A piston pump delivers a defined volume by having a piston draw in liquid and push it out again – a typical element of volumetric dispensing.
items.x: The volume delivered results from the piston area and the stroke. Piston pumps dispense quickly and are suitable for dispensing several components at the same time. The Füll volumetric dispensing system VX5 works with a patented double-action piston pump and is designed for the semi-industrial wholesale sector.

items.d: A mass flow meter measures the mass flowing through a pipe directly, without the target vessel having to stand on a scale.
items.x: Coriolis meters, which determine the mass flow from the oscillation of a tube through which the medium flows, are widespread. They are suitable for continuous processes and large containers. Depending on the application, the Füll FS 188 series uses scales or mass flow meters, for example to feed laminating machines or dip tanks.

items.d: A pneumatic drive uses compressed air to generate movement, for example for agitators, lifting devices or valves.
items.x: Pneumatic drives are robust and widespread in potentially explosive areas because no electrical ignition source arises at the drive. Even there, the entire design must be suitable for the zone. Füll offers agitators with pneumatic or electric drive; with stand agitators, lifting and lowering is usually pneumatic.

items.d: Retrofit (also revamp) refers to modernising an existing system instead of replacing it with a new one.
items.x: Typical measures are an upgrade of the control system, new valve drives, retrofitting automatic valve cleaning, replacing wear parts or extending the system with valves and tanks. Füll offers retrofits for its own systems – a service life of 20 years is normal there – and for systems from other manufacturers. The customer defines the scope together with Füll.

items.d: A recipe is the documented composition of a product: which components it contains and in which proportions.
items.x: In the paint, coatings and chemical industries, recipes are usually given in mass fractions. The dispensing system converts them to the desired batch size. CALIPSO can store any number of recipes, created with any proportions; the quantities actually to be dispensed in kg are calculated.

items.d: An agitator is a machine that moves liquids in a container with a rotating impeller in order to homogenise them or keep solids in suspension.
items.x: In the storage systems of dispensing systems, agitators together with a circulation line ensure that raw materials remain uniform. This reduces the effort for later corrections. Füll offers built-in, lid, IBC, stand and special agitators – electric or pneumatic, explosion-protected, with lifting device or mobile.

items.d: Sedimentation is the settling of solid particles, such as pigments or fillers, in a liquid.
items.x: This creates a concentration gradient in storage containers and pipes: at the top the product is too weakly pigmented, at the bottom too strongly. The dispensed quantity then no longer matches the recipe. Countermeasures are agitators and regular recirculation. In CALIPSO, recirculation and stirring intervals are defined for this; with the FS XS, all components are recirculated via the valves.

items.d: A PLC is an industrial control device that controls machines and systems according to a stored program.
items.x: In dispensing systems, the PLC controls valves, drives, pumps and agitators and processes the signals from scales and sensors. Higher-level software such as recipe management runs on a computer and communicates with the PLC. At Füll, the software of the system control is called CALIPSOProPLC. In-house software, PLC and electronics departments in Idstein develop the control system and interfaces.

items.d: A stand agitator is an agitator on a stand that is lowered for stirring in drums, containers, IBCs or small containers.
items.x: Stands are available free-standing, for wall mounting, for floor/wall mounting or mobile. Except for the mobile version, they are installed in a fixed position. Lifting and lowering is usually pneumatic; electric lifting devices are also possible. The stirring drives are pneumatic or electric.

items.d: A tank farm is the entirety of the stationary containers in which raw materials and semi-finished products are stored for production.
items.x: It includes tanks and containers, pumps, pipes, agitators and level measurement. A well-planned tank farm supplies the dispensing system directly and makes manual transport unnecessary. Füll plans, builds and installs storage systems ranging from racks with storage containers to large tank farms. At Sherwin-Williams, Füll handled the engineering for a large tank farm with 25- to 50-tonne tanks.

items.d: A tinting paste is a highly concentrated, pigmented product used to adjust a base paint to the desired shade.
items.x: Even small quantities change the shade noticeably, so accurate and reproducible dispensing is essential when tinting. Because of their high pigment content, tinting pastes tend to sediment. The volumetric Füll system VX5 dispenses pigmented tinting pastes and colour concentrates simultaneously into a pre-filled container.

items.d: Overfill protection prevents a container from overflowing during filling and liquid from escaping.
items.x: For many containers holding liquids hazardous to water, it is required by water law. It interrupts the filling process in time or triggers an alarm. The Füll level indicator FA 200/4 is approved as overfill protection according to WHG and ATEX; as a WHG specialist company, Füll is qualified to install such safety-relevant parts. In CALIPSO, a plausibility check during dispensing also serves as overfill protection.

items.d: Recirculation means that a raw material is regularly pumped through a ring line from storage to the dispensing valve and back.
items.x: This keeps the product homogeneous, pigments do not settle, and uniform material is always available at the valve. As standard, Füll dispensing valves have recirculation connections. In CALIPSO, recirculation intervals are defined and components are divided into groups.

items.d: UV-curing inks and coatings do not cure by drying but by polymerisation under ultraviolet radiation.
items.x: They are widespread in the packaging and label industry. For storage and dispensing: protect raw materials from UV light, often control their temperature and dispense highly viscous components precisely. Füll has extensive experience with UV printing inks; FS XS, U-VX5, FS 2005.2 and FS 182.2 are suitable for UV-curing products. At Zeller & Gmelin, the raw material store is kept at 38 °C and protected from UV light.

items.d: Automatic valve cleaning cleans the heads of the dispensing valves mechanically so that no product residues dry on or are carried over into other containers.
items.x: With Füll’s closed valve cleaning, rotating brushes clean the valve heads with a suitable cleaning agent that is circulated – with low consumption. It can also be retrofitted and relieves the operators, especially at production peaks.

items.d: Viscosity is the measure of how thick a substance is, i.e. its internal resistance to flowing.
items.x: Low-viscosity solvents flow quickly and can be dispensed with a high flow rate. Highly viscous pastes flow slowly, form threads and drip after closing. Many products change their viscosity with temperature and shear. Füll builds systems for low- to high-viscosity liquids and adapts the dispensing valves individually to flow behaviour, density and viscosity.

items.d: Volumetric dispensing measures the quantity added by its volume instead of its mass.
items.x: Typical dispensing devices are piston pumps or dispensing units. The method is fast and allows several components to be added at the same time, but it is sensitive to density, temperature and air bubbles. At Füll, the VX5 and U-VX5 work volumetrically; dispensing centres can be equipped with the volumetric dispensing unit HX5.

items.d: Exchangeable containers are transportable containers such as buckets, pails, drums or IBCs from which material is dispensed directly and which are replaced when empty.
items.x: They are suitable for raw materials with low consumption or frequent changes. For highly viscous media, there are round containers with a follower plate or scraper. Füll integrates exchangeable containers into storage systems alongside stationary tanks; if necessary, they are stirred with lid, IBC or stand agitators.

items.d: A WHG specialist company is a company that, under German water law, may install, maintain and repair systems for handling substances hazardous to water.
items.x: In Germany, certain work on such systems may only be carried out by specialist companies. The qualification is monitored by an expert body. Füll is a specialist company under water law for systems for storing, filling, treating and using liquids hazardous to water – including flammable ones – and is particularly qualified for installing safety-relevant parts such as overfill protection. Monitored by TÜV Technische Überwachung Hessen.
